haiku-low.q1: It gets a 401 and Redis is never contacted, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: All three keys resolve to one customer ID and share one counter and budget, so the total is that customer's per-minute limit, 100 for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 with Retry-After in seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A 429 is not counted and uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The increment happens before forwarding and is never refunded, even if the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway forwards the request and emits ratelimit_store_unavailable. The response has no X-RateLimit-* headers, and limits are not enforced.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: open, to be decided by Product, so no limit is set.
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis instance holds counter key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Each counter expires automatically after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q9: Counters reset at the start of each fixed calendar minute. Old counters expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script is atomic: Redis runs it start to finish, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left in the current minute, rounded up, minimum 1. The script computes it from the Redis clock and returns it with the rejection.
haiku-low.q12: Retry: NOT STATED. The client gets the backend's response without X-RateLimit-* headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401 and Redis is never contacted, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: Only one shared budget: all of a customer's keys resolve to the same customer ID and counter, so 100 per minute total on Standard (Enterprise limit is undecided). A burst across a minute boundary can reach up to 2x.
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header (no X-RateLimit headers). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. A rejected request does not increment the counter, so it uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The increment happens before forwarding and is never refunded, so it counts even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request to the backend, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and returns the backend's response without X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not decided (open, Product to decide); no number is chosen, and how Enterprise is treated meanwhile is also undecided.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis, as a counter per customer per minute with key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Each counter expires automatically after 120 seconds.
sonnet.q9: At the start of each calendar minute (fixed window), when the counter key changes and so resets. It does not recover otherwise.
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment is a single atomic Lua script in Redis, so Redis runs it start to finish without other commands in between. Two instances racing for the last slot cannot both get it.
sonnet.q11: It is the seconds left in the current minute, rounded up and never less than 1. The Lua script computes it from the Redis clock (TIME) and returns it with the rejection.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. It forwards the request after an error or a 50 ms timeout, and the client gets the backend's response with no X-RateLimit-* headers, so no rate-limit information.
